newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada sees frost on SW Prairie on cold front move.
newsitem.headline: Canada sees frost on SW Prairie on cold front move.

text.p: Canada's Prairies saw frost in some southwestern areas but the northwest likely avoided any frost despite an in coming cold front because of insulating cloud cover, Environment Canada said.
"I'd say there was frost in some parts of Alberta but not in northern Alberta, there's cloud all over," meteorologist Rick Walls told Reuters.

Spring Bank recorded an overnight low of -2.0 Celsius (28.4 F) at chest level, Calgary reported a low of 1.0 Celsius (33.8 F) at chest level and Val Marie, in southwest Saskatchewan, saw a low of 2.0 C (35.6 F) at 0700 CDT.
Temperatures at ground level can be 2.0 to 5.0 C lower than at chest level depending on cloud cover, wind speed and moisture.
Skies were clear over the southwest Prairie as a cold front tracked through Alberta into Saskatchewan and should reach Manitoba late Friday or early Saturday, Walls said.
About half of all cereals and a quarter of canola were harvested in the south by Wednesday, crop reports said.
Northern Alberta reported overnight lows of 3.0 C (37.4 F) in Edmonton and Edson but cloud and rain insulated crops there from frost, he said.
The rest of the Prairies saw overnight lows ranging from 3.0 to 9.0 C, Walls said.
Frost was not indicated elsewhere in Saskatchewan or Manitoba, he added.
Central and southern Alberta should see sunny skies and highs of 15 to 18 C Friday.
Saskatchewan should see a mix of sun and cloud with highs of 15 to 19 C.
Manitoba should see showers and thundershowers with highs of 17 to 23 C.
